newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end lower on oil price rise fears.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end lower on oil price rise fears.

text.p: Delhi shares closed lower in thin trade on Tuesday on selling ahead of an anticipated increase in the state-controlled prices of some petroleum products, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index closed 3.18 points down at 761.35 after peaking at 766.44 in early trade.
"The market is unlikely to stage any rally in the near future as it has been lacking any morale-boosting developments for investors," said Ashok Kaul of brokers Rajpaul Chadha and Co.
Brokers said foreign investors were hesitant about entering the market until the government took a decision on raising oil prices.
On Sunday, strong resistance by left-wing parties prevented the ruling United Front from reaching a consensus to raise prices of some oil products to plug a mushrooming oil-subsidy bill.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral has promised to take a bold decision to tackle mounting losses due to a government subsidy paid to oil firms.
State Bank of India dropped 1.50 rupees to 303.10.
